papers.title_in_file: A benchmarking procedure for quantum networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (Results), Section V (simulations), Section VI (statistics, first part) and Section VII (conclusion). Derivations in Sections II to IV skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of network benchmarking, a randomized-benchmarking-based protocol for estimating the fidelity of a quantum network link, with theory and Netsquid simulations.

assertions.value: The authors propose network benchmarking, adapted from randomized benchmarking, as a procedure that estimates the average fidelity of the effective quantum channel modeling a quantum network link.
quotes: We propose network benchmarking: a procedure to efficiently benchmark the quality of a quantum network link connecting quantum processors in a quantum network.
by yielding an estimate of the average fidelity of the effective quantum channel modeling a quantum network link
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper argues the estimate relates to average fidelity under assumptions and checks it only in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: A protocol proposal, not yet run on real network hardware (the conclusion lists that as a next step).

assertions.value: The authors report that in a Netsquid simulation of n nodes in a linear configuration, with n from 2 to 6, the network fidelity decreases from 0.899 at two nodes, and that it empirically decays exponentially with the number of nodes.
quotes: we performed multi-node network benchmark on n nodes in a linear configuration, where n ranges between 2 and 6
From this we can infer that the network fidelity decreases from 0.899
We note that empirically the network fidelity decays exponentially with the number of nodes
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulation study with modeled noise.
assertions.reader_inference: The six-node value is in the source but its quote carries a plus-minus sign, so it is left out here.

assertions.value: The authors state that network benchmarking is not device independent and that its fidelity estimate rests on assumptions, the central one being Markovian noise: the noise in the link is always modeled by the same quantum channel, independent of the history of its use.
quotes: Network benchmarking is not a device independent protocol, and in order to guarantee that it outputs an estimate of the fidelity of the quantum network link we have to make several assumptions on the behaviour of the nodes and network link.
The central assumption we make is that of Markovianity: we will assume that the noise in the network link is always modeled by the same quantum channel, independent of the history of its use.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope and assumptions, Section III.

assertions.value: The authors argue, with an admitted non-rigorous argument, that multiplicative accuracy for the fidelity estimate cannot be achieved when the number of state transmissions is the cost metric.
quotes: In particular we will argue that we can not achieve
The argument below is not strictly rigorous as we will be making standard statistical assumptions such as normality of distributions
assertions.certainty_reason: Argued with standard statistical assumptions, not rigorous by the authors' own account.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid quantum tensor networks for aeroelastic applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, methods summary lines, Section 3 results and discussion, Section 4 conclusion. Tensor-network background sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: An application study of hybrid tensor-network plus variational-quantum-circuit models for time-series classification and regression on aeroelastic data.

assertions.value: The authors report that their hybrid quantum tensor network solved the binary classification task perfectly and achieved promising results for the time series multivariate and univariate regression tasks.
quotes: We could solve the binary classification task perfectly, and achieved promising results for the time series multivariate and univariate regression tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one aeroelastic dataset, run in simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: Perfect classification is on a binary task from one domain dataset; it does not show an advantage over classical models, which the paper does not compare here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the computations used the Quimb library for tensor networks and PennyLane for quantum circuits and simulations, with 5-fold cross validation for each hyperparameter configuration.
quotes: The computations were performed using the Quimb [32] library for TNs, PennyLane [33] for quantum circuits and simulations
For each hyperparameter configuration, a 5-fold cross validation was carried out
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 2.4 and Section 3.
assertions.reader_inference: Results come from simulated circuits, not quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that regression was considerably more challenging than classification, that the multivariate model captured only certain aspects of the data, and that the optimal choice of hyperparameters remains a challenge.
quotes: The regression task proved to be considerably more challenging than the classification task.
the model was able to capture only certain aspects of the data, but not everything necessary for performing all three regressions at once.
Although, the optimal choice of hyperparameters remains a challenge.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observations from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum walks on graphs embedded in orientable surfaces
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, statements of Theorems 3.1 and 4.1. Proofs and examples skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A mathematical paper on a quantum walk model (the facial quantum walk) whose dynamics reflects a graph's 2-cell embedding in an orientable surface.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a quantum walk model that reflects the 2-cell embedding on the orientable closed surface of a graph in the dynamics, and show that the scattering matrix is obtained from the faces overlapping the boundary and the stationary state from counting two classes of rooted spanning subgraphs of the dual graph.
quotes: A quantum walk model which reflects the 2-cell embedding on the orientable closed surface of a graph in the dynamics is introduced.

We show that the scattering matrix is obtained by finding the faces on the underlying surface which have the overlap to the boundary and the stationary state is obtained by counting two classes of the rooted spanning subgraphs of the dual graph on the underlying embedding.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.1 (scattering matrix) and Theorem 4.1 (stationary state) are stated with proofs.
assertions.reader_inference: Pure mathematical physics of quantum walks; no ML or algorithmic workload is evaluated.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scattering matrix can be obtained from only the information on the external facial walks which pass through the boundary vertices.
quotes: Interestingly, the scattering matrix can be obtained by only the information on the external facial walks which pass through the boundary vertices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.1 decomposes the scattering matrix over external facial walks.

assertions.value: The authors state that the walk is defined on a graph with tails receiving inflow and radiating outflow, and that its dynamics is determined by the abstract graph, the rotation from the embedding, the place of the tails and a unitary matrix H.
quotes: In this paper, we treat such a quantum walk model on the graph with tails receiving the inflow and radiating the outflow
the rotation which is determined by the 2-cell embeding on the orientable surface, the place of the tails
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the model it treats, Section 1.

papers.title_in_file: Connecting ansatz expressibility to gradient magnitudes and barren plateaus
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Theorem 1 and 2 statements and discussion, numerics section, Discussion. Appendix proofs not read.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper bounding the variance of cost-function gradients in terms of ansatz expressibility, extending the barren plateau result beyond exact 2-designs, with supporting numerics.

assertions.value: The paper proves bounds on the variance of the cost partial derivative in terms of the expressibility of the ansatz, for a generic cost function and a layered ansatz, extending the barren plateau result beyond exact 2-designs.
quotes: Specifically, we calculate the variance in the cost gradient in terms of the expressibility of the ansatz, as measured by its distance from being a 2design.
Theorem 1 establishes a formal relationship between the gradient of the cost landscape and the expressibility of the ansatz used.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (and Theorem 2), with proofs in the appendices.

assertions.value: The authors state that their bounds indicate highly expressive ansatze exhibit flatter cost landscapes and therefore will be harder to train.
quotes: Our resulting bounds indicate that highly expressive
exhibit flatter cost landscapes and therefore will be harder to train.
assertions.certainty_reason: An implication the authors draw from upper bounds, not itself a proved lower bound on gradients.
assertions.reader_inference: The bounds are upper bounds, so the claim is a tendency read off them; the Discussion says the bounds are not perfectly tight.

assertions.value: The authors report that their numerics typically showed a strong correlation between expressibility and the variance of the gradient, especially for local cost functions, and that the bounds are not perfectly tight.
quotes: we typically observed a strong correlation (especially for local cost functions) between the expressiblity and the variance of the gradient. However, the bounds are not perfectly tight.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical results for specific cost functions and ansatz choices.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical results are problem specific, and that for highly correlated circuits the variance in the gradient can be larger than their bounds allow, since the bounds were derived for uncorrelated circuits.
quotes: We remark that the numerical results presented here are necessarily problem specific, since they depend both on the choice in cost function and ansatz.
for highly correlated circuits the variance in the gradient can in fact be larger than allowed by our bounds which were derived for uncorrelated circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limits, Discussion and footnote 2.

papers.title_in_file: Predictive Models from Quantum Computer Benchmarks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section IV.A and IV.C-D case studies, Conclusions. Sections II-III on framework details skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A framework of capability models fitted to quantum benchmarking data to predict circuit performance, with an error-rates-model case study and a ResNet50 transfer-learning case study.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a general framework for building predictive models from benchmarking data using capability models.
quotes: we introduce a general framework for building predictive models from benchmarking data using capability models.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of its framework, Abstract and Section II.

assertions.value: The authors report that an error rates model with best-fit error rates had a mean absolute error of 3.0% on ibmq montreal random circuit data, whereas using IBM's reported error rates gave 11.8%.
quotes: of our twoparameter ERM with best-fit error rates is 3.0% whereas if we use IBM's error rates it is 11.8%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one device and one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that a ResNet50 transfer-learning capability model had moderate prediction accuracy on test data, worse than custom de novo CNNs trained on data from the same dataset.
quotes: The trained ResNet50-based capability model (EResNet50) has moderate prediction accuracy on the test data.
However, EResNet50's prediction accuracy is worse than has been obtained using custom de novo CNNs trained on data from this dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one simulated dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports the test error as 2.48% (Fig. 4 caption), but that quote carries a symbol I could not copy safely.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ResNet50 demonstration used simulated data, circuits simulated with a stochastic Pauli errors model, and that only the final dense layer weights were updated in training.
quotes: The circuits were simulated with a stochastic Pauli errors model
Throughout training, only the weights in the final single-unit dense layer were updated (all the weights in ResNet50 were frozen).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section IV.D.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum adversarial metric learning model based on triplet loss function
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 3 simulations and robustness accuracy. Method derivations in Section 2 skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A proposed quantum adversarial metric learning (QAML) model with a triplet loss, simulated on MNIST and Iris.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulation results show the QAML model can effectively distinguish samples of MNIST and Iris datasets, and that adding adversarial samples to the training set improves robustness compared with the QML model.
quotes: Simulation results show that the QAML model can effectively distinguish samples of MNIST and Iris datasets and has higher
Compared with the QML model, the QAML model improves the robustness by adding the adversarial samples to the training set.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on two small datasets by the model's own authors.

assertions.value: The authors report robust accuracies of 92% for the QML model and 100% for the QAML model on MNIST, and 91% and 95% on Iris.
quotes: The -robust accuracies of the QML and QAML models in MNIST dataset are 92% and 100%, respectively.
The -robust accuracies of the QML and QAML models on Iris dataset are 91% and 95%, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result on two small datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: The robustness threshold (0.02) and the epsilon symbol are not in these quotes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the MNIST experiment used only digits 0 and 1, reduced to 2-dimensional vectors by PCA, with 100 samples in each of the training and test sets, in the PennyLane framework.
quotes: so only two categories of handwritten digits, '0' and '1', are chosen to form data sets.
the QAML model first reduces samples into 2-dimensional vectors using the principal component analysis (PCA) method.
The training and test sets contain 100 samples, respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 3.
assertions.reader_inference: Binary classification on two PCA features is a very small test; it does not speak to larger tasks.

papers.title_in_file: TreeVQA: A Tree-Structured Execution Framework for Shot Reduction in Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 7 and 8 (setup and main results), Conclusion. Sensitivity and ablation sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A tree-structured execution framework that runs similar variational quantum algorithm tasks jointly and branches as they diverge, to cut the number of measurement shots.

assertions.value: The authors report that TreeVQA reduces execution shot counts by 25.9× on average, and by over 100× in large-scale applications and diverse settings, while meeting the same fidelity targets as baseline VQA.
quotes: Our evaluations show that TreeVQA reduces execution shot counts by 25.9× on average, and by over 100× in largescale applications and diverse settings, all while meeting the same fidelity targets as baseline VQA.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own simulated benchmarks.
assertions.reader_inference: Savings are relative to the authors' baseline of independent VQA tasks with equal shot allocation; large-scale cases are simulated.

assertions.value: The authors introduce TreeVQA, a hierarchical execution framework that clusters VQA tasks for joint execution and adaptively branches into independent instances only as tasks diverge.
quotes: We introduce TreeVQA, a hierarchical execution framework that clusters VQA tasks for joint execution and adaptively branches into independent instances only as tasks diverge.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of its framework, Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work focuses on VQE and QAOA and that TreeVQA is evaluated with Qiskit simulators, with a statevector simulator used for noiseless simulations.
quotes: This work focuses on VQE and QAOA.
For noiseless simulations, we utilize the StatevectorSimulator to obtain exact quantum state distributions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope and setup, Sections 2.1 and 7.4.
assertions.reader_inference: Results are from simulation, not quantum hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Finitely Repeated Adversarial Quantum Hypothesis Testing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Theorem 1 statement, numerical results, Conclusion. Proof body skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on a passive quantum detector facing an adversary under repeated observations, with an error-bound theorem, numerics and a quantum radar case study.

assertions.value: The authors derive that, under the assumption that the attacker adopts separable optimal strategies, the worst-case average error bound converges to zero exponentially in terms of the number of repeated observations.
quotes: Under the assumption that the attacker adopts separable optimal strategies, we derive that the worst-case average error bound converges to zero exponentially in terms of the number of repeated observations
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, Section 3, proved from quantum Stein's lemma and quantum Sanov's theorem.

assertions.value: The authors report numerically that the naive detector achieves a miss rate and a false alarm rate both exponentially decaying to zero given infinitely many quantum states, although the miss rate decays to zero at a much slower rate than a quantum non-adversarial counterpart.
quotes: given infinitely many quantum states, although the miss rate decays to zero at a much slower rate than a quantum non-adversarial counterpart
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical illustration for the authors' chosen attack model.

assertions.value: The authors state that their quantum radar application is conceptual and that a hands-on implementation would require specifying the radar systems with further details.
quotes: In addition, we have shown a conceptual application of our formulation in studying adversarial attacks on target detection systems using quantum radars.
It is promising to investigate a hands-on implementation of our framework to enhance the security of radar systems if we specify the radar systems with further details.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of the limit, Section 5.
